description: O11 (REFACTOR over STRUCTURE): reorder, duplicate, re-point whoever uses it as a type, and delete - all on an inherited structure. The base is job:structure-lifecycle, so ProductCard (formerly ProductSummary) already has 3 attributes (Title, Price Decimal, Sku), and the type of the Summary output of the public server action Product_GetById, and the expressions 'Summary.Title' and 'Summary.Price' of the Assign SetSummary write its fields. It measures four things: (A) `move` of a structure attribute changes the position in the Attributes sequence and returns the order that remained - in O11 the get of IStructureAttribute does NOT expose IndexInParent, so the position is read in the 'order' field of the move itself and in the dump, never in the get; (B) `duplicate` of a structure copies the attributes in the new order (all-new keys, name with the platform suffix 'ProductCard2'), and in O11 the copy INHERITS Public True and the Description of the original - unlike ODC, where it is born private - and is born without author consumers (only the IAttribute of its own anonymous record 'ProductCard2 Record'); (C) `replace` of one structure by another of the same interface re-points ALL external direct non-derived consumers: the Summary output, the two expressions AND the IAttribute of the anonymous record 'ProductCard Record' (measured: consumers 4, rewired 4, stillPointingAtFrom 0, consumersOfTo 5), and the anonymous record of the original is renamed 'ProductCardCopy Record' because its name derives from the type it points to; the expressions do not change text and Verify stays clean because the copy has attributes with the same names; (D) `delete` of an attribute without consumers is accepted without force (brokenConsumers 0), and the delete of the original structure after the replace ALSO passes without force, because the replace took the anonymous record with it and the source was left with real usages 0 - which is the difference compared to ODC, where the IAttribute of the anonymous record stays at the source and requires force. The refusals with consumers are in tests/jobs-negative/delete-structure-attribute-in-use.json and delete-structure-in-use.json.

ops._why: (0) BEFORE, the inherited order: Title, Price, Sku (positions 0, 1, 2). Three OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructureAttribute; keep the three keys, the dump (1e) must repeat them in another order.

(1a) BEFORE: the attribute that is going to the start. In O11 the properties of the get of an IStructureAttribute are ObjectKey, DataType, Name, Label, Description, IsMandatory, Length, Decimals, DefaultValue, ParentStructure... and there is NO IndexInParent - the position is not read here. Keep the ObjectKey and the Digest: the get (1c) must repeat them.

(1b) CHANGE 1 - REORDER: the attribute moves to the start of the Attributes sequence. Measured: moved 'MoveToStart', order ['Sku','Title','Price'] - the move returns the ORDER that remained, and that is how the position is read in O11. Only the position changes; the key, the type and the consumers stay.

(1c) AFTER: strictly equal to the get (1a) - the same ObjectKey, the same Digest, the same DataType, the same Description. Reordering touches no property of the attribute; that is why the get does not serve to prove the order and the dump (1e) does.
(1d) the relative form: Price now follows Sku. The sibling has to be a child of the same parent. Measured: moved 'MoveAfterSibling', order ['Sku','Price','Title'].
(1e) AFTER, the order: Sku, Price, Title - the SAME 3 keys as the dump (0), in another order. It is the order of the record columns and of the JSON contract of whoever exposes this type.

(1f) the output consumer does not know the order changed: the DataType is still the key of ProductCard (@kAMMFJvTW0CYRFgKFq1T8g in this run - the key changes from run to run, what matters is that it is the same as in dump 0). Keep it: the get (3c) must bring ANOTHER one.

(2a) CHANGE 2 - DUPLICATE the structure (the Ctrl+D of Studio). Measured: 'ProductCard2' is born - the suffix is from the PLATFORM, not the job -, with parent Headless_CS, iface OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructure and a new key. The alias $copy exists because THIS job created it.

(2b) the copy: Name 'ProductCard2', Attributes 3, Fields 3, and - unlike ODC - Public True and the Description of the original ('Resumo de produto. Editado por structure-lifecycle.json.') copied as they are. In O11 the duplicate copies the sharing; whoever does not want it public has to close it by hand.
(2c) the 3 attributes copied in the NEW order of the dump (1e) - Sku, Price, Title -, with all-new keys: the copy does not share a single object with the original.

(2d) count 1, real 1, and that 1 is the IAttribute 'ProductCard2' of the anonymous record 'ProductCard2 Record' that the platform generated with the copy (the kernel does not classify it as derived). From the author: zero - whoever used the original keeps using the original.

ops.name: ProductCardCopy
ops._why: (2e) give the copy an author name; the platform suffix is not a name. Measured: consumers 1 (the anonymous record), expressionsRewritten 0. rename works because IStructure publishes a writable Name.

(2f) idempotent in O11 - the get (2b) already said Public True -, but it stays written because it is the PRECONDITION of the replace (3b): the action Product_GetById is public and an output type of a public action has to be public. In a clone that does not inherit the sharing, this set is what avoids the Verify refusal.
(2g) AFTER: Name 'ProductCardCopy', the SAME key as the get (2b), Public True, Attributes 3.

(3a) BEFORE the replace: the 4 inherited consumers - IOutputParameter Summary, the two IExpression #Variable ('Summary.Title', 'Summary.Price') and the IAttribute 'ProductCard' of the anonymous record 'ProductCard Record'. count 4, real 4.

(3b) CHANGE 3 - RE-POINT: the same ReplaceReferences as in Studio, from and to of the SAME interface (IStructure), without force. Measured: consumers 4, rewired 4, stillPointingAtFrom 0, consumersOfTo 5, scope 'direct-external-nonderived'. The 4 touched: the two IExpression, the IOutputParameter Summary AND the IAttribute of the anonymous record - which appears in the list already with the path 'IAnonymousStructure:ProductCardCopy Record/IAttribute:ProductCardCopy', because the name of the anonymous record derives from the type it points to. What the replace does NOT do: map the children - the expressions still cite Summary.Title and Summary.Price by name, and the copy has attributes with those same names, so Verify stays clean.
(3c) AFTER: the output DataType now points to the key of ProductCardCopy (the one from the get 2b), not to the one from the get (1f). The SAME parameter ObjectKey, another type underneath.

(3d) count 0, real 0: the source was left WITHOUT consumers - not even the anonymous record, which in O11 the replace took with it. Compare with the usages (3a) and with the ODC version of this job, where the IAttribute of the anonymous record is left behind and forces the delete (4c) to use force.

(3e) count 5, real 5: the 4 consumers of the usages (3a) with the SAME keys (the output, the two expressions and the IAttribute agE0TNfn.. of the anonymous record of the original, now named 'ProductCardCopy Record'), plus the IAttribute of the copy's own anonymous record (907Mk5gG.., from the usages 2d). Two anonymous records with the same name pointing to the same type: it is the cost of a structure replace in O11.
(3f) the expressions did NOT change text: 'Summary.Title' and 'Summary.Price' are still the same - they never cited the type name, and the output is still named Summary.
(4a') BEFORE deleting: count 0, real 0 - no expression writes Summary.Sku. It is the right attribute to prove the delete without force.

(4a) CHANGE 4 - DELETE an attribute WITHOUT consumers: accepted without force, brokenConsumers 0. The refusal of the delete of an attribute WITH a consumer (Name, written by 'Summary.Name') is measured in tests/jobs-negative/delete-structure-attribute-in-use.json.
(4b) AFTER: 2 attributes (Price, Title) where the dump (2c) showed 3; the keys of those that remained are those of the dump (2c). The Summary output has just lost a field without an op touching it.

(4c) DELETE the original structure after it was re-pointed, WITHOUT force: the usages (3d) already said real 0, and the delete confirms brokenConsumers 0. In O11 there is no platform-generated consumer holding the source after the replace - the anonymous record went to the copy -, so force is neither needed nor present here. The refusal of the delete of a structure with author consumers is in tests/jobs-negative/delete-structure-in-use.json.

ops.name: ProductCard
ops._why: (4d) empty list: the structure disappeared, and no object in the module answers to 'ProductCard' - the anonymous record that had that name has been called 'ProductCardCopy Record' since the replace.

(4e) AFTER the delete of the source: measured count 5, real 5 (IAttribute 2, IOutputParameter 1, IExpression 2) - the SAME list as the usages (3e). The anonymous record that was born with ProductCard was NOT deleted with it: the replace had re-pointed it to the copy and renamed it to 'ProductCardCopy Record', and the delete of the source left it orphaned. Two anonymous records with the same name remain, pointing to the same structure; it is the trace that a structure replace+delete leaves in O11, and it is only read here.

ops.name: ProductCardCopy
ops._why: (4f) THREE objects answer to the name: the IStructure ProductCardCopy (OutSystems.Model.Data.IStructure) and TWO IAttribute 'ProductCardCopy' (OutSystems.Model.Types.IAttribute), one per anonymous record - the copy's own and the original's orphan. It is the pair of the find (4d), which returned zero.
(5) END: the public action still exposes 1 input and 1 output, Nodes 4, now typed by ProductCardCopy (public), and the module is valid - Verify reports nothing.
